question: Can native self-sensing and training on consequences of the graph's own proposed writes improve new-life learning and immediate A retention?

comparisons.sensing-baseline: additional own local activation and postcommit receipt, matched timing
comparisons.causal-sensing: incremental consequence training for a self-proposed edit
comparisons.causal-shuffled: correct assignment of future consequence compared with shuffled examples

primary_measures: stable noisy new worlds, late realized correct fraction
reversed worlds, realized correct fraction across the first four contacts after reversal
first A-return choice after ABA minus first A-return choice after CBA
secondary_measures: same trained birth, full deployment versus write disabled
win over B-only history on first A return
future realized benefit prediction versus constant zero, conditional direction and prevalence of nonzero targets
single-edit fork crossing committed parameters and postcommit activity
uncertainty: Use paired training births as independent units. For primary contrasts report per-birth results and paired 95% Student t intervals; exact paired sign-randomization p-values are descriptive. Intermediate checkpoints are repeated measures. Secondary contrasts exploratory.
fork_constraints: Future external stimuli, taste noise and random uniforms are shared, future choices and subsequent writes remain autonomous. Deployment never observes the paired trajectory.
